rules.rule: 1 million events per day is about 12 per second.
rules.why: A day has 86,400 seconds, so divide by about 10^5 and adjust. Scale linearly from there.

rules.rule: Peak traffic is commonly 2 to 5 times the daily average.
rules.why: Traffic is not uniform. State your peak factor and design for peak, not average.

rules.rule: Plan servers at around 60 to 70 percent utilisation at peak.
rules.why: Headroom absorbs bursts, failures and deploys. Running at 100 percent leaves no room for any of them.

rules.rule: Replicate important data 3 times unless you can justify less.
rules.why: Three copies tolerate a failure while another is being repaired. Multiply raw storage by the replication factor.

rules.rule: Memory is far faster than disk, and the network is far slower than memory.
rules.why: One datacenter round trip costs about as much as several thousand memory references, so avoid chatty calls.

rules.rule: Each extra nine of availability cuts the allowed downtime by 10 times.
rules.why: 99.9 percent allows about 8.8 hours a year, 99.99 percent about 53 minutes, 99.999 percent about 5 minutes.
